column1: # The candidate ledger separates four things one URL conflates. A model identity
# is what the weights learned. An artifact is one file expressing those weights
# in one value format. A runtime shape is what the loader must support. A role
# is what the appliance would serve the row for. Twenty-two distinct URLs
# reduce to nineteen model identities here, because a safetensors repository and
# its GGUF twin are one identity, and a plain and an i1 GGUF repository of one
# fine-tune are one identity in two artifacts.
# The distinction decides how much device time a row costs. Throughput belongs
# to an architecture and a value format, so five fine-tunes of one architecture
# at one quantization share a throughput class and need one reference arm rather
# than five. Quality belongs to the learned weights, so those same five need
# five graded arms.
# The ledger fills in two phases because its columns have two sources. Every
# column except architecture_fingerprint and chat_template_hash comes from the
# Hugging Face model API. Those two come from the GGUF metadata block, which a
# GGUF places at the head of the file, so remote/admit-candidate-static.py
# reads them over an HTTP range request and the weights stay on the server. A
# populated row therefore rests on a partial fetch of tens of megabytes rather
# than on a local artifact. A safetensors row keeps `-` in both columns because
# it publishes no GGUF header to read.
# `artifact-defective` names a row whose chosen artifact cannot be read as
# published, which is a property of the file rather than of the weights: the 9B
# Defiant Fable MTP artifact carries 4,942,442,720 bytes whose first 10.5 MiB
# are zero, so its magic, metadata block, and tensor index are absent while the
# tensor payload beyond them is intact.
# admission_stage is where a row sits rather than what is claimed about it.
# `served` is already in remote/models.tsv. `static-admitted` has its
# architecture and chat template read from the published header and no device
# time. `phase-1` has its API record alone. `provenance` is a source artifact
# retained for conversion rather than for serving. `excluded` has a checkable
# property that removes it: pipeline sentence-similarity and
# visual-document-retrieval name repositories with no chat path this suite can
# grade. `superseded-by-gguf` names a safetensors repository whose own GGUF
# twin is a separate row, which is redundancy rather than a defect.
# `artifact-absent` names a repository whose pinned revision holds no model
# file at all: the Damien420 0.8B max-distillation pair carries a
# `.gitattributes` alone in both its GGUF and its source repository at the
# revisions read on 2026-08-28, so there is nothing to fingerprint or fetch,
# and the row re-enters admission when a later revision publishes a file.
# preferred_artifact names the file a row's fingerprint speaks for. `-` leaves
# the Q4_K_M preference to choose, which is right across a roster and wrong where
# a row exists for a specific rung: the 9B Defiant Fable row is admitted for its
# two-bit IQ2_M artifact in the multi-token-prediction variant, which the
# repository publishes beside an identically sized artifact without that block.
# conversion_required states whether serving this row needs a format the
# appliance can produce. `yes` means the repository publishes safetensors alone,
# and the appliance holds no torch, so the conversion runs elsewhere or the row
# waits. A `yes` row is a scheduling fact rather than a rejection.
# finetune_lineage is `unverified` where the model card was not read. It is a
# claim about provenance and this file does not assert one it has not checked.
# The six lifecycle columns carry a row from admission toward a serving
# decision. runtime_class is the architecture, embedding width, feed-forward
# width, and head-count group from evidence/model-admission/static-admission.md
# -- the unit throughput belongs to, leaving out block count, which an ordinary
# load skips past the multi-token-prediction block. `-` means no GGUF header
# was read, so no class is known.
# throughput_reference names the candidate_id whose measured decode tok/s
# stands for the row's class, with its evidence file, from
# evidence/model-admission/runtime-class-throughput.md or remote/models.tsv. A
# row that is itself the class's measured member, or a served row, carries `-`;
# a class with no measured member anywhere carries `-`. quality_control names
# the served remote/models.tsv row this candidate is graded against in one
# sweep -- the incumbent of its runtime class -- or `-` where no served row
# shares the class.
# next_test is the one device-time step that moves the row forward:
# `strict-load` (remote/test-strict-vulkan-placement.sh has not yet run this
# artifact), `throughput-arm` (loaded, needs a decode arm inside its class),
# `quality-sweep` (loaded and measured, needs the graded suite), `depth-fill`
# or `projector-depth-fill` (served but its validated_filled_depth gap is
# open), or `none` where no test in this set applies -- a conversion-blocked
# row, a structurally excluded pipeline, a defective artifact, or an already
# served or retired row.
# stop_condition is the measurable criterion that retires the row, stated
# before the arm that would decide it runs, the way
# evidence/research-claim-methodology.md requires a falsifier stated first.
# `-` where the row is already served or has no artifact to test.
# disposition is the row's current standing: `served` is in remote/models.tsv;
# `redundant` names a measured or byte-identical class member elsewhere in
# this ledger carrying the same quality claim, so this row adds none of its
# own; `pending` names a row a next_test still moves; `retired` names a row
# whose stop condition is already met -- an excluded pipeline, a defective
# header, or a served row displaced by tier; `absent` names a row with no
# artifact at the pinned revision.
